create.title: Transition-flattened energy reduced to coherent nonzero residue offsets
create.statement_tex: Let J=sqrt(X), Q=J^(2/5), T=J^(3/5), B=C/T, and J^(13/18)<C<=J^(3/4). For every fixed smooth-interior nonaxial M1 component, local class kappa in {1/4,1/2,1}, alias, and orientation, split the exact transition-flattened principal row into admissible progressions modulo 4b: S_b=sum_(r in R_(kappa,b)) u_(kappa,b,k)(r) R_(kappa,b,k)(r), where the exact odd or even local unit is constant on the progression and R(r)=sum_(c asymp C,c=r mod 4b) V(c)e(plus-or-minus A_(kappa,b)/c). The accepted global-BV symbol and Bourgain reciprocal estimate give |R(r)|<<_epsilon X^epsilon TQ^(-5/24). Hence the complete same-residue energy and every fixed nonzero residue-offset layer are <<_epsilon X^epsilon B^2T^2Q^(-5/12)=X^epsilon C^2Q^(-5/12), target-safe through C<=J^(47/60), in particular throughout the frozen band. The only remaining smooth-main object is X_C=sum_(b asymp B)sum_(r not equal s)u(r)conj(u(s))R(r)conj(R(s)), with target X_C<<_epsilon X^epsilon J^2/T. Absolute accumulation gives only X^epsilon C^3/(TQ^(5/12)). A conditional gain B^(-delta) reaches C<=J^((13/6-3delta/5)/(3-delta)); delta=1/2 reaches J^(56/75) and delta=5/9 closes the first band. In the odd class the zero product-Kloosterman Fourier mode is exactly the safe same-residue part and the nonzero modes are exactly X_C; complete Poisson inversion is an exact self-return. No offset gain, conductor extension, upper-band estimate, cone-edge estimate, full M9-M1, M9, or exponent is proved.
create.next_action: Prove a signed B^(-delta) gain in the coherent nonzero residue-offset sum with the exact local units and reciprocal weights retained. Delta=1/2 gives a nonempty extension to C=J^(56/75); delta=5/9 closes the whole first residual band.

update.statement_tex: Let J=sqrt(X), Q=J^(2/5), T=J^(3/5), and J^(13/18)<C<=J. In the first band J^(13/18)<C<=J^(3/4), the exact transition error and axes are separately target-safe, so only the globally smooth nonaxial principal energy remains. For each fixed local class, alias, orientation, and compatible nonaxial k, split its exact principal row into admissible residue progressions modulo 4b. The complete same-residue energy and every fixed nonzero residue-offset layer are <<_epsilon X^epsilon C^2Q^(-5/12), target-safe through C<=J^(47/60). Thus the first-band principal energy is exactly reduced to the coherent nonzero-offset actual-unit correlation X_C=sum_b sum_(r not equal s)u(r)conj(u(s))R(r)conj(R(s)), with target X_C<<_epsilon X^epsilon J^2/T. Its absolute capacity is X^epsilon C^3/(TQ^(5/12)); a B^(-delta) signed gain is required. On J^(3/4)<C<=J, the principal main, transition error, and axes all require signed control. This proves no estimate for X_C, no new conductor interval, no cone edge, full M9-M1, M9, or exponent.
update.next_action: Attack the coherent nonzero residue-offset actual-unit correlation in J^(13/18)<C<=J^(3/4), seeking any fixed B^(-delta) gain before returning to the upper band where transitions and axes also remain open.
Close the coherent nonzero residue-offset correlation in the first upper-conductor band, then treat C>J^(3/4), cone edges, remaining radial sectors, and endpoint uniformity.

reject.reason: The ordinary Kloosterman large sieve depends only on coefficient L2 mass and has exact capacity BQ^2T=B J^2/T. The common square-root chirp supplies no saving in a coefficient-uniform theorem.

The current Pascadi and Blomer-Pascadi theorems require a single fixed modulus and two genuinely varying coefficient intervals for their savings. The literal map is a full residue interval against one singleton, while the energy is a varying-modulus product-Kloosterman kernel with a joint symbol.
For moduli 4b the common divisor in Pascadi's modulus-average theorem is only 4, not B. Its literal capacity retains the unsaved modulus factor and does not estimate the product kernel.

Complete Poisson, the chirp-preserving B-process, and the matched Kuznetsov-Voronoi chain reconstruct the original residue row when all lower terms, supports, and tails are retained. An involutive representation change is not an analytic gain.

Switched-cusp Voronoi after level-four newform and oldform decomposition has conductor- and dilation-dependent centers. The raw newform centers include N_f X/4 for N_f in {1,2,4}; no universal X/4 center is justified.
There are O(B) nonzero residue offsets. Each fixed layer is target-safe, but absolute accumulation costs exactly the missing factor B; a signed correlation theorem is required.

no_change.reason: The first residual band is narrowed to a coherent nonzero-offset correlation, but no estimate or conductor extension is proved; upper conductors, cone edges, other radial sectors, and endpoint uniformity remain open.
Round 82 concerns only the M1 transition-flattened upper-conductor principal energy.
Both M9-M1 and M9-M2 remain open.
The round proves a structural M1 reduction but no new global Gauss-circle exponent.

round_assessment.reason: The round does not extend the accepted conductor range, but it rigorously removes the complete same-residue mode and every fixed nonzero offset layer, identifies the coherent actual-unit offset correlation as the strict first survivor, proves transform self-return, and audits all current source maps without overclaiming M9-M1 or the exponent.
